name: science-centre-303
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes. Its one photograph is taken close up through a wide lens that bows the long edges by a few pixels (the pinhole camera's residuals reach 6 px along the bands' gaps), so the principal point is solved too

building.title: Science Centre (303), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 303's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). The site replaces block 303 by its id.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

lidar.licence: Auckland Part 1 LiDAR (2024), OpenTopography NZ24_Auckland, doi:10.5069/G9HH6H8T: sourced from LINZ and licensed by Regional Software Holdings Limited for re-use under CC BY 4.0

aerial.licence: Auckland Central 0.06 m Urban Aerial Photos (2023): sourced from LINZ and licensed by Auckland Council for re-use under CC BY 4.0

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline

ground_note: provisional: the median LiDAR ground (class 2) in the crop box (p5 37.2, p95 46.7: the site falls about 9 m); set to the ground at the door at step 7

light.note: estimated: the photograph is under an overcast sky (no shadows), so the viewer's sun stands behind the building from the south-east (135 deg round, 35 deg up), which leaves the face to the street, the one the photograph shows, in open shade; the exposure from the building's luma: p10/p50/p90 50/152/158 at 2.0 against the photograph's 111/156/200 (126 at 1.4, 142 at 1.75, 148 at 1.9: its dark glazing and gaps hold the p10 down)
